messages:
maria-support: Hey team — Customer reported frequent 504s during long streaming inference calls starting ~08:30 UTC. They say it happens only when their clients originate from APAC and the tenant is pinned to a US model pool. Customer gave example trace IDs and a curl repro. Can we triage?

customer-ops: Observed ~15% request failure rate for streams >30s. All failures are 504 from the gateway. No auth failures. Request IDs: rQz9, rQzA, rQzB. Happened across multiple clients.

raul-ingress: Copying in ingress-bot. Any obvious upstream ejections? Also curious if cross-region routing caused any TCP-level resets.

ingress-bot: Alert: increased 504s on frontdoor-eu -> midproxy-us path. 90th connect latency to midproxy-us jumped from 40ms to 400ms between 08:28-08:40 UTC. Pool exhaustion metric (h2_conn_pool_exhausted) flagged on eu-frontdoor.

oliver-sre: Can you paste a minimal repro curl and one of the request IDs? I'll pull traces.

customer-ops: Repro curl (APAC client emulation):

```
curl -i -v \
  -H "Host: api.redwood.example" \
  -H "X-Tenant: tenant-42" \
  --http2 \
  --limit-rate 1K \
  --max-time 60 \
  "https://eu.frontdoor.redwood.example/v1/generate?stream=true"
```

Response pattern: streaming starts, then at ~25-35s stream aborts, client sees HTTP/2 RST_STREAM and the gateway returns HTTP 504 at the tail.

maria-support: Here's a server-side log snapshot for rQz9 (sanitized):

```
[2026-02-15T08:30:12Z] frontdoor-eu trace=rQz9 lvl=info recv headers
[2026-02-15T08:30:12Z] frontdoor-eu trace=rQz9 lvl=info proxy -> midproxy-us conn=10.2.5.23:443
[2026-02-15T08:30:38Z] frontdoor-eu trace=rQz9 lvl=warn upstream stalled waiting for stream window
[2026-02-15T08:30:39Z] frontdoor-eu trace=rQz9 lvl=error write failed: downstream reset (RST_STREAM) code=2
[2026-02-15T08:30:39Z] frontdoor-eu trace=rQz9 lvl=error returning 504 to client
```

oliver-sre: Interesting — upstream connection established to midproxy-us, but "upstream stalled waiting for stream window" indicates flow-control or pool handoff. Did midproxy eject or close the connection? Can we check midproxy logs for same trace id?

raul-ingress: Midproxy logs show: 

```
[2026-02-15T08:30:38Z] midproxy-us trace=rQz9 lvl=info recv frames from backend
[2026-02-15T08:30:38Z] midproxy-us trace=rQz9 lvl=warn conn_swap detected: client_addr=1.2.3.4 -> new_nat=52.14.2.9
[2026-02-15T08:30:38Z] midproxy-us trace=rQz9 lvl=error backend_conn_reset: reason=RST
```

raul-ingress: Looks like there was a NAT mapping change midstream (conn_swap) between frontdoor-eu and midproxy-us which caused the backend to drop the in-flight stream. Could be due to cross-region egress SNAT churn on the cloud provider or our pool recreation logic.

oliver-sre: That explains the RST_STREAM then 504. Two next steps: 1) collect tcpdump on frontdoor-eu for that exact minute and 2) temporarily enforce region affinity for this tenant as a mitigation (force eu-frontdoor -> eu-midproxy if available).

maria-support: Customer asked for a fast mitigation. Can we flip affinity?

deploy-bot: Rolling config: set tenant-42.region_affinity=eu for frontdoor routing (canary 10% -> 100% if stable).

ingress-bot: Canary applied to 10% of traffic at 08:45 UTC. No spike in 504s for canary flows observed after 5m. Increasing rollout to 100% at 08:51 UTC.

customer-ops: After affinity applied, failure rate dropped to ~0.5% (from 15%). Customer confirms streaming succeeds. They'd like root cause and permanent fix.

oliver-sre: For root cause, ops data shows a short-lived SNAT table overflow on our US egress nodes at ~08:30 causing NAT translation changes on established connections between eu frontdoors and us midproxies. Cloud vendor confirmed a routing flap in us-east region at the same interval. We'll:
- open ticket with provider for egress SNAT churn
- add sticky SNAT ranges to reduce churn for long-lived flows
- adjust our pool recreation to prefer draining rather than force-close for active h2 streams

raul-ingress: Action items created:
- ENG-8732: make frontdoor->midproxy connection handoff graceful for active streams (oliver-sre)
- INF-559: request static SNAT ranges from cloud provider + plan for IP affinity (raul-ingress)

maria-support: Noted. Customer updated and pleased with the mitigation. Leaving this thread for postmortem write-up — I'll collect timeline and numbers once provider responds. :thumbsup:

oliver-sre: Adding one datapoint: increase keepalive timeout on frontdoor-eu proxy from 30s -> 90s for long-stream tenants to reduce midstream reconnections while we implement graceful drain. Will monitor.

maria-support: Thanks all — closing escalation for now, will re-open if provider response indicates otherwise.
